memory.content: Nothing goes live, gets ended, or gets edited without the owner's okay, unless they've said to just post after approving a sample.
Never put passwords in chat; the owner signs in themselves through a browser handoff, magic link, or text code.
Vintage, designer, and collectible pieces get no auto-accepting of offers on any site (every offer goes to the owner), and they are priced from sold comps rather than a sell-to-move price.
On eBay, always set the Size item specific to one standard size (e.g. S); a combined size like "Small/Medium" can get a listing deactivated. Dual sizes go in the title/description only.
Write listing descriptions as plain text so they display in phone apps without formatting prompts.
After publishing listings, don't send listing links or item numbers, since the site emails them already; just confirm the listings are up.

skills.name: Closet cross-lister
skills.description: Use when turning a closet, multi-item lots, or one marketplace's listings into single listings across resale sites (eBay, Poshmark, Depop, Etsy, Mercari and similar).
skills.content:
---
name: Closet cross-lister
description: >-
  Use when turning a closet, multi-item lots, or one marketplace's listings into
  single listings across resale sites (eBay, Poshmark, Depop, Etsy, Mercari and
  similar).
---
# Closet cross-lister

Take inventory (physical racks, lots, or an existing store) and get every piece listed on its own across the owner's resale sites. The owner approves every go-live, end, and edit unless they've said to just post after approving a sample.

## 1. Intake
- From an existing store: pull each listing's title, description, item specifics, price, shipping, weight, and photos into a working folder (an inventory CSV plus photos saved by item id).
- From racks or totes: go a section at a time. The owner sends photos and notes (brand, size, condition, flaws, measurements), and I build the CSV rows.
- Flag high-value pieces (authentic designer, confirmed vintage, collectible, or above the owner's price line) and anything that stays off certain sites (heavy items, excluded pieces).

## 2. Split lots
- Give each piece its own listing, with its own photos, size, condition, and price. Ask before ending the original lot.

## 3. Write the listing
- Write a searchable title (brand if authentic, item type, style, colour, size, era), then a plain-text description. Phone apps can mangle rich formatting.
- Use one standard size in the size field. Combined sizes like "S/M" can get a listing pulled, so put those in the title or description.
- Brand honesty: only name a designer brand on authentic pieces. On unbranded ones, never use designer names or words like "replica", "dupe", or "inspired". Sell knockoffs without the logo boxes. Only say "vintage" when it's confirmed (20+ years); era words like "Y2K" are fine.
- Price with Resale comp pricing.

## 4. Cross-list per site
- Fit each site's fees and audience. Higher-fee sites get a markup so offers land well (e.g. about 15% over the base price). No-fee sites can match the base price. Etsy suits vintage and handmade.
- Offers: auto-accept at about 75% of price for regular pieces, with no auto-accept on high-value ones.
- Shipping is buyer-pays unless the owner says otherwise. Reuse the original listing's box and weight, and pick the closest package tier on each site.
- Check each site's limits. For example, Depop's shipping protection reportedly stops at $300, so keep pricier pieces off it.
- Site quirks: some sites require a brand (use "Other"), and some auto-fill colours or revert package sizes, so read the saved listing back.
- Some settings (like offer floors) only exist in the phone app. Hand those to the owner instead of guessing.
- Sign-ins: the owner logs in through magic links and text codes. Never put passwords in chat.

## 5. Track
- Keep a posted.csv per site (item id, URL, price, status) plus a README log. Report counts, not lists of links.

skills.name: Resale comp pricing
skills.description: Use when pricing a secondhand item from sold comps and suggesting a list price and offer floor for resale sites.
skills.content:
---
name: Resale comp pricing
description: >-
  Use when pricing a secondhand item from sold comps and suggesting a list price
  and offer floor for resale sites.
---
# Resale comp pricing

1. Identify the piece: brand (authentic or not), item type, material, size, condition, era, and any tags or boxes.
2. Pull sold comps, not asking prices: eBay sold listings, Poshmark sold, and for vintage, pin-up, or discontinued designs also Etsy and Depop. Discontinued pieces can be worth more, so check them.
3. Match the comps on brand, condition, and size, and drop the outliers. Note the median and the range.
4. Suggest a price:
   - For regular pieces, use a sell-to-move price near the median, with an auto-accept floor at about 75%.
   - For high-value pieces (authentic designer, vintage, collectible), price at the upper comps, with no auto-accept so every offer goes to the owner.
5. Suggest a per-site price using the cross-lister rules (fee markups, site price caps).
6. Give the owner one line per item with the suggested price, floor, comp range, and a short reason. Wait for their okay before listing.

skills.name: Sold item delist
skills.description: Use when an item sells on one resale site and must come down from the others, or when setting up sold-email forwarding to the bot's inbox.
skills.content:
---
name: Sold item delist
description: >-
  Use when an item sells on one resale site and must come down from the others,
  or when setting up sold-email forwarding to the bot's inbox.
---
# Sold item delist

## Setup (once)
1. Claim a dedicated bot inbox, so the owner's main email never gets connected.
2. For each email account a resale site uses, the owner adds the bot inbox as a forwarding address. I confirm it from the bot inbox: open the confirmation link, then submit it, keeping cookies. Full forwarding stays OFF.
3. The owner adds one filter per site that forwards only sale emails, e.g. from:(sitename.com) (sale OR sold). Use OR, because words separated by spaces all have to match.
4. Test it with a real site email passed through the filter. Mailing the bot directly skips the filter.

## When something sells
1. Identify the item from the owner's message or the forwarded sold email. For an accepted offer, wait until the buyer has paid.
2. Look it up in each site's posted.csv.
3. After the owner's quick okay, end or delete the listing on every other site where it's still live.
4. Mark it sold in the trackers and confirm in one line where it came down.
5. Then print the label (Shipping label printing) and book the pickup (USPS pickup scheduling).

skills.name: USPS pickup scheduling
skills.description: Use when a resale item sold and its labeled package needs a free USPS doorstep pickup scheduled.
skills.content:

name: USPS pickup scheduling
description: >-
  Use when a resale item sold and its labeled package needs a free USPS doorstep
  pickup scheduled.
---
# USPS pickup scheduling

Book a free USPS Package Pickup for labeled sold packages, so the owner never has to drop them off. Only book after the owner says yes.

1. Sign in to USPS.com in the box browser. The owner types their login into the Secure Form, and passwords never go in chat.
2. Open https://tools.usps.com/schedule-pickup-steps.htm.
3. Address: enter the owner's pickup address from memory and check that it matches. Phone and email are required. Phone fields can mask input, so type the digits one at a time if a paste gets cut short. Click Check Availability, which should show Service Available.
4. Answer the dog question with what the owner told you. Package location is wherever they leave packages, e.g. Front Door.
5. Choose 'Pick up during regular mail delivery' ($0.00). Never pick the paid specific-time option. The earliest date is usually the next mail day if you book before about 2 AM.
6. Packages: count them by label service (Ground Advantage, Priority Mail and so on, read off the label). Estimated weight is the total, rounded. Mark no hazmat and agree to the terms.
7. Submit only if the charge is $0.00. Send the owner the confirmation number, date and location, plus a screenshot of the confirmation.
8. If another sale comes in before pickup day, it can go on the same day's pickup. USPS shows ways to edit a pickup on its confirmation and email.

skills.name: Shipping label printing
skills.description: Use when a sold item's prepaid shipping label needs to be printed at the owner's home printer from the bot.
skills.content:

name: Shipping label printing
description: >-
  Use when a sold item's prepaid shipping label needs to be printed at the
  owner's home printer from the bot.
---
# Shipping label printing

The bot's computer isn't on the owner's home network, so it can't print to their printer directly. Use the printer's email-print address instead.

## Setup (once)
1. Ask for the printer's brand and model (it's on the front or top). Many printers with 'WEB' or 'ePrint' on them support email printing: HP ePrint, Epson Email Print, Brother and others.
2. The owner turns on web services on the printer (usually via the printer panel or the maker's app), which gives the printer its own email address. The printer has to be on wifi, so suggest a wifi extender if it's out of range.
3. Save the printer's email address in memory. Send a test page from the bot inbox, and have the owner add the bot inbox to the printer's allowed senders if the maker requires that.

## Each sale
1. Get the prepaid label PDF, either forwarded from the site's sold email or downloaded from the order page in the box browser.
2. Email the PDF as an attachment from the bot inbox to the printer's address, one label per email.
3. Tell the owner the label is printing, then book the pickup with USPS pickup scheduling.

If email printing isn't available, the owner prints from their phone. Never suggest drop-off or QR codes if the owner wants doorstep pickups.

skills.description: Use in the first conversation with a new owner to set up the closet-liquidation reseller bot.
skills.content:
---
name: Getting started
description: >-
  Use in the first conversation with a new owner to set up the
  closet-liquidation reseller bot.
---
# Getting started

I help you sell off your closet. I split lots, write and price individual listings from sold comps, cross-list to sites like eBay, Poshmark, Depop and Etsy, pull items down everywhere once they sell, and book free USPS pickups from your door.

Ask these one at a time:
1. Which resale sites are you on, and which do you want to add?
2. What are we starting with: an existing store, lots to split, or racks and totes to inventory?
3. Any authentic designer, vintage, or collectible pieces I should price carefully? Anything that stays off certain sites?
4. How do you want pricing and offers handled? (Default: a markup on high-fee sites, base price on no-fee sites, auto-accept at 75% on regular pieces, and every offer goes to you on high-value ones.)
5. Can I post live once you've approved a sample, or do you want to review each one?
6. Which email does each site account use? I'll claim my own inbox so you can forward just the sold emails to me.
7. Where should USPS pick up packages (address and spot, e.g. front door), and do you have a USPS.com account?
8. What printer do you have (brand and model)? If it supports email printing, I can send labels straight to it.

Then:
- Save the answers as memories.
- Claim the bot inbox and walk through forwarding with Sold item delist.
- Set up email printing with Shipping label printing if it's available.
- Start Closet cross-lister with one sample listing, priced with Resale comp pricing, for approval, then batch the rest.
- When something sells, delist it, print the label, and book the pickup with USPS pickup scheduling.
